theme: Spotlight and Handoff: user activities and searchable items

terms.definition: An object that describes what the user is doing in your app, so the system can resume it later.
terms.example: Create an NSUserActivity for the open article.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let activity = NSUserActivity(
    activityType: "com.example.read")
activity.title = "Reading Swift"
print(activity.title ?? "")

terms.definition: A feature that lets the user continue an activity on another Apple device, such as from iPhone to Mac.
terms.example: Turn on handoff for the reading screen.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let a = NSUserActivity(activityType: "x.read")
a.isEligibleForHandoff = true
print(a.isEligibleForHandoff)

terms.definition: An item that you add to the Spotlight index, so users can find your content from system search.
terms.example: Add each article as a CSSearchableItem.

video.description:
Learn to explain how an app lets users continue on another device and find content in search: NSUserActivity, Handoff & CSSearchableItem, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
NSUserActivity - An object that describes what the user is doing in your app, so the system can resume it later.
Handoff - A feature that lets the user continue an activity on another Apple device, such as from iPhone to Mac.
CSSearchableItem - An item that you add to the Spotlight index, so users can find your content from system search.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain NSUserActivity, Handoff and CSSearchableItem in English?

dialogue.title: Continue on my Mac
dialogue.setting: Making articles easy to resume and find

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users want to continue reading on their Mac after they start on the iPhone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then describe the reading with an NSUserActivity. It tells the system what the user is doing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `a` is the NSUserActivity for our article?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Set the `title`, and call `becomeCurrent` when the screen appears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And what makes it move to the Mac?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Handoff. Set `isEligibleForHandoff` to true, and the Mac shows the app icon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It needs nearby devices that use the same Apple account.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can people also find our articles from search?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Add each article as a CSSearchableItem in the Spotlight index.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is a CSSearchableItem the same as an NSUserActivity?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. The item is searchable content, and the activity is something the user is doing.

dialogue.code:
import Foundation
let a = NSUserActivity(activityType: "x.read")
a.title = "Swift Tips"
a.isEligibleForHandoff = true
a.becomeCurrent()
